scope: Operational writing baseline for the existing 50 chapters, 435 sections, 19 reader routes and seven volumes; not a claim of completed prose, proof review, reader validation or a scholarly edition.
body_policy: This baseline change writes planning only. Subsequent body work follows the queue and section-local start checks; all-series external review is not a condition for starting the first draft. Publication acceptance remains separate.
research_policy: No new standalone paper audits. Existing source-audit records are archived reference material. Verify only the exact claims needed for the section being drafted; a disputed optional hardware claim is qualified or omitted without blocking unrelated chapters.

change_policy: Editorial clarification, typo fixes and improved examples may preserve the baseline when scope, prerequisites, proof obligations and volume placement remain unchanged.

A dependency, section split/merge, depth change, central-result/scope change, new topic or volume reassignment needs an impact record, stable-ID/anchor migration if relevant, a new baseline version and regenerated queue. Never silently downgrade a proof to meet a page budget.

Priority changes need a versioned batch amendment and a fresh dependency check. Page ranges are planning envelopes, not typeset promises; significant expansion is assessed against reader workload and proof completeness.
Correct mathematical or safety-critical claims immediately, record affected sections/examples and revalidation; do not preserve a known error merely to keep the baseline unchanged.
section_acceptance: A filled brief names the concrete question, entry/exit skills, exact prerequisite IDs, result/scope and P/F/M/R/V obligation, local notation, complete-example or justified non-code role, independent check, source target and problem/answer plan.

The draft defines every new symbol before use, supplies local mathematical/physical bridges, explains central intermediate steps, and points to the exact imported result. A central argument cannot be hidden in an exercise or dismissed as obvious.

Mathematical review checks the exact result and assumptions at the frozen depth. Numerical tests validate an implementation, not a theorem. An R section must include its local special-case proof/lemmas and name what is deferred.

Code-bearing sections have a complete executable program, formula-to-code correspondence, pinned environment, expected output/tolerance and an independent reference. Actual FlagQuantum support and execution are recorded; missing APIs use the upstream gap workflow and never remove required theory. A non-code section records why code is not appropriate.

Each section includes at least one worked example or justified conceptual/model case, one local comprehension/prediction checkpoint and one transfer/failure-analysis task with an accessible answer/hint path. A chapter closes with conceptual, derivation/proof, implementation and debugging problems as appropriate; exact counts are calibrated after the opening batch.

A target reader attempts the argument and a transfer task. Record the missing step, repair and recheck. Before acceptance record mathematical, implementation or justified N/A, and reader reviews separately with evidence. Accepted prerequisites are required for publication; an explained working draft can support the next draft.
section_start_checks: Use the next scheduled stable section ID and its existing result/proof/source record; complete the brief before writing prose.

Every imported earlier result has a usable draft with definitions and matching conventions, or a bounded local bridge is supplied and scheduled. Known blocking errors in an imported result are resolved first.
Inspect the exact source target needed for this section; fix or qualify a material uncertainty locally. A generic whole-book source review is not required.
Choose the independent small reference and the worked/transfer cases; investigate an API only when its actual use is imminent. No new validated-execution claim is made without a run.
